brief: September's 54bp rise in 10y Treasury yields was 49bp real yields versus 5bp breakevens, read as investors demanding higher after-inflation returns, not more inflation protection, a different emphasis from the Fed reaction-function concerns raised after July's FOMC. The author frames the move as markets repricing growth persistence and the real rates needed to accommodate it, driven by fiscal easing, loose financial conditions and AI investment competing for capital. Financing persistent deficits alongside AI capex requires more saving or a higher real return. He is wary of calling a durable yield top but equally wary of extrapolating the selloff: further upside needs fresh repricing of growth, policy or term premia. Stronger growth can support equity earnings even as higher discount rates compress valuations. Stable breakevens signal confidence the Fed will deliver needed real-rate hikes, not that inflation is solved. August core PCE eased to 0.2% MoM but held at 3.0% y/y, and September ISM prices-paid jumped to 77.9. Markets price 3-4 more hikes, which he calls reasonable. Cheaper AI broadens adoption but makes standalone frontier development harder to monetize than the compute complex, keeping him most bullish on hyperscalers, distinguishing owning the frontier from owning the economics of its deployment.
